aspects.says: datesUntil excludes its end date, so a period given by its first and last day needs last.plusDays(1), while a range that already ends on an exclusive date needs nothing added.
basis: section:datesUntil Leaves Out Its End Date

aspects.says: The last day of a month comes from TemporalAdjusters.lastDayOfMonth() or the month's length, not from a fixed day number; whether a date is a month end depends on its month and year.
basis: section:The Last Day of a Month Comes From an Adjuster, Not a Day Number

aspects.says: A LocalDateTime is a wall-clock reading with no zone; the same value converted with two zones gives two instants, and Instant.from refuses it.
basis: section:A LocalDateTime Is a Wall-Clock Reading, and the Same One in Two Zones Is Two Moments

aspects.says: LocalDate.parse and LocalDate.of refuse a date the calendar doesn't have, and parse also refuses single-digit fields and trailing text; nothing clamps or rolls over.
basis: section:LocalDate.parse and LocalDate.of Refuse Dates That Don't Exist

aspects.says: plusMonths clamps the day to a shorter month's last day and forgets the original day, so chained month steps drift and don't reverse; each date of a series is computed from the first one.
basis: section:plusMonths Clamps to a Shorter Month's Last Day, So Step From the First Date

aspects.says: withDayOfMonth sets the day and throws DateTimeException for a day the month doesn't have, rather than clamping.
basis: section:The Last Day of a Month Comes From an Adjuster, Not a Day Number
